fact_text: The speaker said the Pakistani stock market is highly cyclical: strong years are needed to make up for weak ones, and the average return of about 18% a year is only earned across the full cycle.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said a realistic long-run return for Pakistani equities is about 18% a year, and that expecting a single strong year of about 50% to repeat is an unrealistic expectation that drives investor losses.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said the market fell in June 2025 on Iran-related events and shares became cheaper afterwards, but many investors had stayed out and did not buy the dip.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said a textile company typically makes money in about 3 of every 10 years, and spends the other 7 years surviving the downturn.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said chemical companies typically earn in about 3 of every 10 years, with the other 7 years spent surviving the downturn.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said cement companies typically earn in about 4 of every 10 years, with the other 6 years spent surviving the downturn.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said a broker earns commissions on each trade, so its advice can be swayed toward buying or selling, while an advisor paid on a client's long-term portfolio has an incentive aligned with the client's long-term gains.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said an advisory or equity fund fee of about 4% a year can, on a small portfolio over two to three years, take a share of value comparable to the client's whole portfolio, so paid advice only pays above about 80 lakh rupees.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker's rule of thumb was that paid stock advisory only makes sense for a portfolio above about 80 to 90 lakh rupees, and the speaker said an advisor's fee of about 4% on a crore-sized portfolio is about 4 lakh rupees a year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker warned that an investor with about 1 lakh rupees may want to put 40 lakh rupees into the market on borrowed money to chase quick gains, which turns a fall in prices into a loss far larger than the original capital.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)

fact_text: The speaker said taking more risk does not guarantee more money, it only raises the chance of loss, and investors should weigh both their own capacity to absorb losses and the cyclical risk of the market.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Where Stock Investors Go Wrong — InvestKaar CEO Explains | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-23)
